playbooks.title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting
playbooks.methodology: Inject a unique marker into each reflected parameter, then check whether it returns in the response unencoded and in an executable context (HTML body, attribute, or script). Escalate from a benign tag marker to context-breaking payloads only to confirm the sink.
playbooks.remediation: Context-encode all user input on output (HTML entity, attribute, JS, URL encoding as appropriate) and deploy a strict Content-Security-Policy. Prefer framework auto-escaping; never build HTML by string concatenation.

playbooks.title: SQL Injection (error + boolean)
playbooks.methodology: Start with a single quote and parenthesis-breakout variants to surface database errors across MySQL, Postgres, SQLite/Sequelize (Node), Oracle and MSSQL. If no error, use a boolean-differential pair (always-true vs always-false) and compare response length/status. Never use destructive payloads (DROP, DELETE, UPDATE).
detect_signatures: you have an error in your sql syntax
playbooks.remediation: Use parameterized queries / prepared statements or a vetted ORM; never concatenate input into SQL. Apply least-privilege DB accounts and allow-list identifiers (table/column names).

playbooks.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference
playbooks.methodology: Object-reference parameters must be tested with TWO authenticated identities: fetch an object as user A, then request the same id as user B. A match proves broken access control. A scanner cannot confirm this alone — flag for auth-context validation.
playbooks.remediation: Enforce server-side authorization on every object access (verify the current user owns/may access the id). Use unpredictable identifiers and deny-by-default access checks, not client-supplied ids alone.

playbooks.title: Open Redirect
playbooks.methodology: Set redirect-control parameters to an external canary host and inspect the Location header on 3xx responses. Confirm the canary host appears in Location.
playbooks.remediation: Do not use user input to build redirect targets. Allow-list permitted destinations or use mapping keys; if external redirects are required, show an interstitial and validate the host against an allow-list.

playbooks.title: Server-Side Request Forgery
playbooks.methodology: URL-accepting server-side fetch parameters should be tested with an out-of-band (OOB) collector canary; confirmation requires observing the inbound request at the collector. Without an OOB listener a scanner can only flag the surface — mark for OOB validation.
playbooks.remediation: Allow-list outbound destinations, resolve and validate hostnames, block internal/link-local ranges (169.254.0.0/16, 127.0.0.0/8, metadata endpoints). Disable unused URL schemes and follow-redirects.

playbooks.title: Server-Side Template Injection
playbooks.methodology: Inject a math marker the template engine would evaluate (e.g. {{7*7}} -> 49). A reflected '49' where the literal was sent proves evaluation. Keep payloads arithmetic-only; never call engine internals.
playbooks.remediation: Never pass user input into template source. Use logic-less templates or sandboxed engines, and pass user data strictly as bound context variables, not as template strings.

playbooks.title: Path Traversal / LFI
playbooks.methodology: File/path parameters may allow traversal. Request a well-known read-only file via traversal sequences and look for its signature in the response. Read-only probing only; never write or include remote resources.
playbooks.remediation: Resolve and canonicalize paths, then confirm they stay within an allowed base directory. Reject traversal sequences and absolute paths; prefer opaque file identifiers mapped server-side.

playbooks.title: Missing Security Headers
playbooks.methodology: Inspect the origin's response for the baseline hardening headers. This is an origin-level property — report once per origin, not per URL.
playbooks.remediation: Add Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options (or CSP frame-ancestors), Strict-Transport-Security, and X-Content-Type-Options at the edge/app for every response.
